clue.text: Robber once found in the infantry quarters

parts.note: foot soldiers are the infantry, collectively 'foot'
a pad is slang for one's lodgings or quarters

explanation.surface: A highwayman of old is discovered hiding in the soldiers' barracks.
explanation.walkthrough: A footpad was a robber who worked on foot rather than on horseback, hence 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: A footpad was a highway thief operating on foot in earlier centuries, an archaic word for a street robber.

clue.text: Floor in a numbered apartment?

parts.note: a flat is an apartment
a flat with a number, here ten

explanation.surface: Asking which storey a numbered apartment is on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Floor' reads as a storey, but it is the verb meaning knock down.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor someone is to knock them down level, to squash them.

clue.text: Strange dealer in the House doing casual work

definitions.note: describes the person, so it stands for a noun: one who does casual work

parts.note: odd means strange
a jobber was a dealer on the London Stock Exchange, known as the House

explanation.surface: An odd trader at the Exchange takes on casual work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the House' looks like Parliament, but it was the nickname for the London Stock Exchange, where jobbers dealt in shares.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd-jobber is a handyman taking on casual, miscellaneous tasks.

clue.text: Sports area that's perfect for some noted players

definitions.meaning: the playing field in football or cricket
musicians with perfect hearing of notes have absolute recognition of tone

explanation.surface: A ground that is ideal for well-known sportspeople.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noted players' reads as famous athletes, but means musicians reading notes; perfect pitch is identifying a note by ear.
explanation.definitionFit: A playing field is the sports sense, and musical tone the sense in 'perfect' hearing of notes.

clue.text: Ousted physicist is first accommodated by theologian

indicators.note: being accommodated by someone means being housed inside them

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian

indicators.note: first tells us to place the word is ahead of the physicist

parts.note: Sir Oliver Lodge was a British physicist and radio pioneer

explanation.surface: A scientist is the first to be put up by a theologian.
explanation.definitionFit: Dislodged means removed from a position, forced out.

clue.text: It divides the staff from top to bottom!

definitions.text: It divides the staff from top to bottom!

parts.words: It divides the staff from top to bottom!
parts.note: reads like a company split from boss to junior, but the staff is the musical stave, crossed vertically by a line marking off each measure

explanation.surface: Something causes a rift through every level of an office workforce.
explanation.definitionFit: In written music a vertical stroke crosses the five-line stave to separate one measure from the next.

clue.text: Clumsily move a boat

definitions.meaning: a flat-bottomed cargo vessel on canals

explanation.definitionFit: Lumbering forward is to push about heavily, and a flat cargo vessel on canals is the craft.

clue.text: Criticise theatre company getting female in debt

parts.note: rep is short for repertory company

indicators.note: getting means receiving, so one piece takes the other inside

parts.note: in the red means in debt
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: A repertory company employs an actress while it is losing money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the red' is overdrawn, so 'in debt' gives RED.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprehend is to rebuke or reprove someone.

clue.text: Hibernal problem causing some panic in Gatwick?

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Winter weather causes a scare at a London airport.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'causing', which is a link word; 'Hibernal problem' alone matches the noun. Gatwick is a London airport, where ice on wings grounds planes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice forming on aircraft wings in winter is a known hazard, a cold-season trouble.

clue.text: School principal follows urge to become an intellectual

indicators.note: follows means comes after, so the principal is placed behind the urge

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them
a head is a headteacher

explanation.surface: A headteacher gives in to an impulse to become a highbrow.
explanation.definitionFit: An egghead is informal for a bookish, highbrow person.

clue.text: University involved in entrance examination

indicators.note: being involved in something puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: an adit is a horizontal entrance to a mine

explanation.surface: A university's admissions exam.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is a formal inspection of accounts, a kind of official scrutiny.

clue.text: Young fellow shy about hallucinogenic experience

indicators.note: about here means going around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: to shy is to throw, as is to sling
a trip is a drug-induced hallucinatory episode

explanation.surface: A bashful lad has a bad drug episode.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shy' looks like an adjective for the young fellow, but it is the verb meaning throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripling is a youth not yet fully grown, a lad.

clue.text: Also, half of this (not all) is appetising

parts.note: too means also

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is its first two letters

parts.note: some means a part, not the whole

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about only part of a dish being tasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothsome food is tasty and pleasing to eat, delicious.

clue.text: Hound shakes off black bird of prey

indicators.note: shaking something off means losing it, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a beagle is a breed of hound
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A dog fends off a dark raptor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black bird' reads as one phrase, but black is the B to be removed.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle is a large raptor that hunts by day.

clue.text: Plutocrat rejected an old coin

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a bob was the British shilling, a coin worth twelve old pence

explanation.surface: A wealthy man turns down a coin of former times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns only AN, giving NA; a bob was a pre-decimal British shilling.
explanation.definitionFit: A nabob is a man of great wealth, originally one who made a fortune in India.

clue.text: A musical inamorato

definitions.meaning: Sandy Wilson's 1950s musical comedy about 1920s flappers

explanation.definitionFit: Sandy Wilson wrote a 1953 stage show of that title, and a male sweetheart is the second sense.

clue.text: Like some old books reliable as an investment

definitions.meaning: fine old volumes have page edges gilded
describes very safe securities, such as government stock

explanation.surface: Antique volumes described as a safe financial bet.
explanation.definitionFit: Antique volumes often have gold-leafed page edges, and the same term describes safe government securities.

clue.text: Adam helps new lighting director

indicators.note: new means remade, so the letters form something fresh

explanation.surface: A man named Adam assists a fresh theatre lighting designer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lighting director' sounds like a stage job, but it is a shade that directs a lamp's light.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade over a bulb directs and softens the light, so it is jokingly a director of illumination.

clue.text: After midnight a French athlete becomes a smuggler

indicators.note: after says the remaining pieces follow the first

parts.note: the middle of the word night is G
un is French for a
a runner is an athlete

explanation.surface: Late at night a French sprinter turns contrabandist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' is the middle letter of 'night', G.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunrunner smuggles weapons illegally.

clue.text: Extremely dim Tory disturbed by month of torment

indicators.note: by here means beside, so the month stands next to the rest

parts.note: Mar is the abbreviation for March

indicators.note: disturbed means stirred up, so these letters are rearranged
extremely takes the outermost letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A stupid Conservative is upset by a month of suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dim Tory' reads as an insult to a politician, but 'Extremely' trims dim to its outer letters before 'disturbed' shuffles them with the party name.
explanation.definitionFit: Martyrdom is great suffering, death or torture endured for a belief.

clue.text: Drink supplier — a very good friend of the songwriter

definitions.meaning: one who delivers bottles to the doorstep

definitions.text: a very good friend of the songwriter
definitions.meaning: a song title calls the doorstep delivery man 'my very good friend'

explanation.surface: A drinks deliverer is close to a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: The milkman delivers a drink each morning; the old song lyric is 'my very good friend the milkman'.
explanation.definitionFit: A milk roundsman delivers bottles to homes, and the Fats Waller song 'My Very Good Friend the Milkman' gives the second.

clue.text: Director-general carrying in old dog

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so one piece contains the other

explanation.surface: A top boss brings in an ancient hound.
explanation.definitionFit: The dingo is the wild canine of Australia.

clue.text: Supervise metrical composition in Old English

indicators.note: in places the composition inside the other letters

parts.note: verse is writing in metre

explanation.surface: Someone directs the writing of an Anglo-Saxon poem.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to watch over and direct work.

clue.text: Delight in returning to the bar?

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to revel in something is to delight in it

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys going back to the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub, but here it is a rigid rod used to prise things.
explanation.definitionFit: A lever is a rigid rod pivoted to shift a load, a crowbar being one.

clue.text: Malice of churchman with high honour

parts.note: Ven is Venerable, the title of an archdeacon
OM is the Order of Merit, a high British honour

explanation.surface: Spite from a highly decorated cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: An archdeacon is styled 'the Venerable', abbreviated Ven.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom is spiteful bitterness, poisonous ill will.

clue.text: Weariness of Scottish girl embracing unlimited study

indicators.note: embracing means hugging, so the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: a lassie is a girl in Scotland

indicators.note: unlimited means losing the bounds, so the word's first and last letters go

explanation.surface: A Scots girl tires of endless studying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlimited study' sounds like endless revision, but 'unlimited' simply removes the word's first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassitude is physical or mental tiredness, a lack of energy.

clue.text: Crazy game upset youth leader

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: pool is a cue game

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A mad sport throws a young captain.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' turns a word upside down, reading it bottom to top; pool is the cue game played in bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Loopy is informal for mad or eccentric.

clue.text: Pastoral poem is faulty, with extremely dreary content

indicators.note: content here means contents, what is held inside

parts.note: ill can mean bad or defective

indicators.note: extremely takes the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A rural verse is poor and very dull throughout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' reads as an adjective meaning happy, but here it is the noun: the contents held inside the word for faulty.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll is a short poem describing rustic life.

clue.text: State nominates characters for new assembly

indicators.note: a new assembly means the letters are put together afresh in another order

explanation.surface: A US state picks candidates for a fresh legislature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' says it is the letters of 'nominates' that are reassembled.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnesota is one of the fifty United States, in the upper Midwest.

clue.text: King not seen in an American city for ages

indicators.note: a part not seen in a word is dropped from it

parts.note: Yonkers is a city in New York State
ER is Edward Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: A monarch is absent from a US city for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: ER usually means the Queen, but here it is Edward Rex. YONKS is informal British for a very long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonks is British slang for a very long time, as in 'I haven't seen her for yonks'.

clue.text: Arrange to be married on this festive occasion?

definitions.text: Arrange to be married on this festive occasion?

parts.words: Arrange to be married on this festive occasion?
parts.note: to fix a wedding date is to 'name the day', and a saint's feast celebrated by those sharing the saint's name fits the festive occasion

explanation.surface: A couple choose a holiday for their wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A name-day is the feast of the saint one is named after, celebrated like a birthday in many countries.

clue.text: Expatiate and blow up

definitions.meaning: to expatiate is to speak or write at length on a subject

explanation.definitionFit: To expand on a topic at length and to make a print bigger are both senses of magnifying.
